name: ECMWF Open Data (IFS and AIFS real-time forecasts)
owner: European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF)
gives: global weather forecasts (temperature, wind, precipitation rate, pressure and more) from the IFS and AIFS models, four runs a day

why.quote: A subset of ECMWF real-time forecast data from the IFS and AIFS models is made available to the public free of charge. Their use is governed by the Creative Commons CC-BY-4.0 licence and the ECMWF Terms of Use. This means that the data may be redistributed and used commercially, subject to appropriate attribution.
why.basis: licence statement (CC BY 4.0 plus ECMWF Terms of Use); data.ecmwf.int/robots.txt returns 404 (no robots rules published)

interface: Files over HTTPS in GRIB2 at https://data.ecmwf.int/forecasts/YYYYMMDD/HHz/{ifs|aifs-single}/0p25/oper/ (0.25 degree; 0.1 degree files split into -sfc and -pl). Mirrored on AWS, Azure and Google Cloud public buckets. Official Python client: ecmwf-opendata (not run here). No key, no account.
notes: Keyless. Licence page of the Terms of Use (https://apps.ecmwf.int/datasets/licences/general/): attribution must be displayed prominently and include 'this document/data/output/Results is/are based on data and products of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF)'; users must remove attribution if requested; no warranty. Limits stated on the open-data page: portal access limited to between 500 and 2000 simultaneous connections; rolling archive of the latest 12 runs (about 2 to 3 days); the cloud mirrors are recommended for heavy use. No per-IP rate limit found. The page also says accessing or arranging delivery of open data 'may be subject to Service Charges and a Service Agreement' (that concerns delivery services, not the public files; to confirm). Size: global GRIB2 files, tens to hundreds of MB per step, so a collector must cut out a Europe or Portugal box and write small JSON (needs a GRIB reader). Easier keyless forecasts for Portugal exist via Open-Meteo (already in the brief).
